rows.subtype: Family member in a medical emergency [Actor]
rows.description: An adult whose parent collapses feels panic and a rush of decisions about hospital, money and relatives. Calling emergency services first and sorting the rest later keeps the order right.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: An injured or ill person often feels frightened, embarrassed and dependent, and takes comfort from a calm voice and clear simple statements. Being told what is happening reduces fear more than empty reassurance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: fear, embarrassment, calm

rows.description: A schoolchild climbs, runs near roads or plays with fire or sharp things without imagining consequences. Their sense of cause and effect is real but short-range, so adult limits and clear rules matter.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager attempts a dare, a stunt or a fast ride to gain status, knowing the risk but feeling the social reward more strongly. The brain weighs peer approval heavily at this age.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Road and vehicle safety in India [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager rides a two-wheeler without a helmet or with three riders because everyone around does. Local habit makes danger feel normal, and the wise choice needs courage against the crowd.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult travelling or going out alone notices a feeling that something is off and must decide between politeness and leaving. Trusting that early feeling and exiting quietly is sound judgment, not rudeness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: An adult ignores an exposed wire, a gas smell or a shortcut around a safety rule because nothing has gone wrong before. Familiarity dulls alertness, and near misses are the warning that is easy to ignore.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A wise worker reports a hazard or refuses an unsafe instruction calmly, giving specific facts and a suggested fix. Safety problems are cheaper to raise than to explain afterwards.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young child proudly stirs, carries plates or wipes a table, more slowly and messily than an adult would. Feeling useful builds confidence, and patient acceptance of imperfect help teaches more than doing it for them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Making own bag, bed and simple food [Actor]
rows.description: A schoolchild learns to pack a bag, make a bed and prepare something simple like tea or a sandwich under supervision. Small duties build responsibility and awareness of how much home work exists.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
